P1 nine raw casts `*(f32 *)((u8 *)c + offsetof(Critter, floorContact) [+ 4|+ 8])` -> `c->floorContact[0|1|2]` (field authority: `gdlmem.py struct Critter --offset 0x438` returns the GC project header include/game/critter.h line 190 `f32 floorContact[3]; /* 0x438 */`). P2 deleted `result = 0;` before the `if (surface != NULL)` and added `else { result = 0; }` to the flags test, the SlideAlongWall test and the outer test -- four assignment sites, matching the target's four `li r26,<v>`. P3 the same treatment for `grounded`: deleted `grounded = 0;` and added `} else { grounded = 0; }` to the FloorCollide test. P4 inverted the flags test to `if ((... & 0x38) != 0) { result = 0; } else if (SlideAlongWall(...) < 0) {...} else { result = 0; }`. P5 added `f32 *cpos;`, assigned `cpos = c->pos;`, and routed the five later `c->pos` uses (the two CritterWorldDamage arguments, the three `probe[i]` reads, the second `probe[i]` block and the FloorCollide argument) through it. P6 changed `from = cpos;` at the head to `from = NULL;` and moved `from = cpos;` into the `else` branch immediately before the EnemyWallCollide call, and reordered the preamble to `minRise; cpos; from; wallRadius; radius; surface`. P7 swapped `grounded = 1;` ahead of the CritterWorldDamage call. P8 moved `void *surface;` from the head of the declaration list to after `s32 grounded;`. Both `delta[2] = delta[0] = 0.0f;` chained assignments also became `delta[0] = delta[2] = 0.0f;` (inside P2 and P3) to match the target's store order.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Zero builds: `python tools/gdl/savedregs.py game/enemy/critter CritterCollideWorld --per-web`. If `DEFINITION-COUNT DIFFERS on r30 (3 vs 8)` is not reproduced -- if ours ever stops redefining the register whose first definition is `@0x38 li r30,0` far more often than the target does -- then `from` is not the absorbing web and the split targets the wrong variable; re-read the per-web table and re-derive before probing. One build: if the block-scoped loop pointer returns NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, the web split does not reach codegen here and the function should be re-screened as a recolor candidate instead.

The function reached T298/O298 parity during this pass (`COUNT-PARITY GAINED insns T298/O297 -> T298/O298`) with an IDENTICAL 298/298 multiset, which is the whole class gain of the pass; a web split that changes the count forfeits it and would put the function back outside every postprocessor class per claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-a-count-asymmetric-residual.20260831.v1. hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- the aligned views at 0x18:0x60, 0x100:0x134, 0x158:0x1e0, 0x264:0x290 and 0x3c8:0x400 were all read against the retail bytes across this pass, and every register and displacement quoted in this record and its law is quoted at its own defining or using offset in BOTH streams. hypothesis.statement: The remaining 32 words are a LATER-LIVE-RANGE question, not a first-definition one, and the next lane must not spend declaration-order probes on it. `savedregs.py game/enemy/critter CritterCollideWorld` now prints `ASSIGNMENT MATCHES: every callee-saved register holds the same value at its FIRST definition in both streams` across the whole save set (the r25-r31 range and the f25-f31 range), each row byte-identical in both streams -- for example `@0x30 addi r31,r28,92` (the `cpos` web) and `@0x38 li r30,0` (the `from` web) appear at those offsets in target and ours alike. The tool's own escape hatch then fires: `THE SAVE SET IS WRONG IN A WAY THIS TABLE'S ROWS DO NOT SHOW: 1 VOLATILE ROLE PROMOTED IN OURS; 2 LIFETIME ESCAPED TO A VOLATILE`, and the counts line reads `DEFINITION-COUNT DIFFERS on r25 (6 vs 3), r26 (7 vs 6), r27 (6 vs 5), r30 (3 vs 8)` -- whose three low rows are the three zero inits this pass aligned, `@0x4c li r25,0` (surface), `@0x54 li r26,0` and `@0x58 li r27,0` (the hitnode loop's two counters), each now byte-identical and at the same offset in both streams. The load-bearing row is r30: the target defines it exactly THREE times -- `@0x38 li r30,0`, then `@0x10c mr r30,r31` in the else branch, and once more inside the hitnode loop -- while ours defines it EIGHT times, so our `from` web is absorbing later ranges the target keeps separate. The concrete untried lever is therefore to SPLIT the `from` web: give the hitnode loop its own pointer local instead of reassigning the function-scope `from` inside it, so `from` carries exactly the definitions the target's r30 carries and the loop's own pointer becomes a separate short web. That is the block-scope web-split lever of claim.law.GW_block-scope-splits-a-coalesced-copy-but-a-same-scope-copy-folds.20260901.v1, pointed at a web this pass created rather than at one it inherited.
